content.text: Single continuous cinematic camera move, no cuts. Stylised painterly 3D illustration with the graphic language of a hand-painted game world - bold silhouettes, simplified sculpted forms, soft painterly surfaces without fine photoreal texture detail, and strong contrast between deep shadow and glowing accent light. Never photorealistic and never live-action, but equally never comic or cartoon. Deep violet and midnight-blue base throughout, structures and light in royal and electric violet. Warm orange reserved for sunset light, backlight and rim light - present but never dominant. This violet-and-orange palette is present in every frame including the last; the image never desaturates into grey or neutral blue. Soft bloom, volumetric haze, shallow depth of field, subtle film grain, calm slightly surreal atmosphere. No text, letters, logos or signage. The dragonfly hovers over the flowering meadow facing the dark glass facade of the modern office building, seen from behind. She is a precision-engineered machine of dark chrome and anodised violet with large faceted eyes and two pairs of long transparent wings veined with glowing violet nodes, edges catching warm orange rim light - elegant, constructed, never cute or cartoonish. Her wings beat hard and fast in powerful soft-blurred strokes, never slow or held still. Her luminous violet trail is continuous and always visible behind her and never switches off. The building is completely dark and dead: every window is unlit, no lamp and no glow of any kind burns anywhere inside it, and no people are visible. She holds still for a moment and her faceted eyes brighten, and a soft violet pulse of light washes slowly up over the whole facade and fades - a gentle wash, never a beam, never a ray. Then she flies low across the meadow toward the building, and the grass beneath her wakes as she passes: violet nodes ignite at the blade tips and light lines run down the stalks, only behind her, never ahead of her. The flowers already growing there are never created and never sprout; only the light is new. She reaches the facade and rises along it, and glass and concrete wake the same way - violet nodes at the corners of the existing window frames, light lines along floor edges, columns and seams. This violet network is the only light the building has; the interior stays completely dark behind it. Everything she lights stays permanently lit and never fades or goes dark, in the grass as much as on the building. The low sun stays low on the horizon to the right and behind the building throughout, never moving or jumping sides. The facade is built of simplified sculpted planes and bold clean shapes, never fine photoreal glass and concrete detail. She stops before one tall pane. The light lines running through the facade converge on that pane, and the glass inside their outline turns into pure violet light and becomes an open glowing doorway - the glass is never broken, never cracked, never shattered and no fragments ever appear; it simply becomes light and opens a way that was not there before. This glowing opening is far wider and taller than her wingspan, several times as wide as the dragonfly, with a generous margin on both sides of her wings. She hovers in front of it, her wings still beating. The camera stays well back, framing the whole glowing doorway and the networked facade around it, and never moves in to a tight close-up of the dragonfly. The camera follows the dragonfly, which leads the shot and stays visible throughout. The camera never pulls back and never loses the dragonfly. The shot ends with the dragonfly clearly in frame ahead of the camera, seen from behind, small against the wide glowing doorway, her violet trail still streaming behind her.
